definition: Revitalize means to bring new energy and strength back to something that has slowly grown weak, dull, or inactive.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word revitalize. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know revitalize should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Hoping to revitalize the diner's tired menu, the new chef added a dozen colorful dishes that soon had regulars lining up out the door again.
Refresh is weaker than revitalize; a cold drink refreshes you for a moment, but it does not give something whole new life.
Resurrect is stronger than revitalize; you revitalize something that is fading, but you resurrect something that is completely gone.

Rejuvenate means to make something feel young and fresh again — a spa weekend rejuvenates you, a redesign rejuvenates a brand. It restores a youthful feel. Revitalize restores working energy and strength: a revitalized downtown has businesses and foot traffic again, not just a fresher look.

Reinvigorate means to put new vigor into something flagging — a pep talk reinvigorates a tired team. It usually boosts effort, morale, or momentum. Revitalize runs deeper and slower: it brings a fading place, institution, or enterprise back to real strength and life.

Revive means to bring something back from having stopped — a canceled tradition can be revived, and so can a person who has lost consciousness. Revitalize needs no full stop: it pumps fresh energy into something that still exists but has gone flat, like a tired menu or a declining downtown.

Revitalize means to bring new energy and strength back to something that has slowly grown weak, dull, or inactive.
After weeks of drought, a single night of steady rain revitalized the tomato garden, and by morning the drooping vines stood tall and green again.
The vines had grown weak and droopy, and the rain gave them back their strength and liveliness overnight.
Bringing fresh life and energy to something that was fading is exactly what revitalize means.
Common in news writing about places and institutions: people revitalize a downtown, an economy, or a career.
Do not confuse it with revive, which often means bringing someone back to consciousness; revitalize means pumping fresh energy into something that still exists but has gone flat.

For years the Saturday farmers' market in Lindenvale had been shrinking: a dozen stalls where sixty once stood, and vendors who packed up by noon.
The market never closed outright -- a few growers always came -- but everyone agreed it had gone flat.
A new manager set out to revitalize it: longer hours, live fiddle music, a shared oven where bakers sold bread hot from the stone.
She recruited young farms from three counties and gave each a season's stall for free.

Two summers later the lot was full again, and the market pulsed with an energy old-timers said they had not felt in twenty years, though its wooden stalls and hand-painted signs were the same ones as ever.
